_comment: JOE configuration. Edit paths here. Nothing is scanned automatically.

reasoning._comment: The reasoning provider. 'none' means JOE cannot compose answers and says so. Supported: none, claude, m365_copilot, ollama, openai_compatible. NO CREDENTIAL IS EVER STORED HERE. Claude reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from the environment; Microsoft 365 Copilot signs in through MSAL and the token lives in an encrypted Windows cache. Copilot answered in 6.6 and 9.9 seconds on this machine, which is too slow to talk to while driving, and its Chat API is a /beta endpoint Microsoft states is not supported for production use.

copilot._comment: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat API - PILOT / PREVIEW. Requires a work or school account with a Copilot licence, an Entra app registration, and admin consent on seven delegated Graph scopes. Personal Microsoft accounts are not supported by this API. tenant_id and client_id are deliberately EMPTY here and are read from the environment instead - ASSISTANT_COPILOT_TENANT_ID and ASSISTANT_COPILOT_CLIENT_ID. Neither is a secret, but both identify the organisation's Entra directory, and this file is tracked in git. Setting a value here still works and overrides the environment.

claude._comment: Claude, through Anthropic's official SDK. The API key is read from the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable and never appears in this file. fast_mode runs the same model at up to 2.5x the output speed for double the token price - latency is the point for a driver, so it is on by default; set it false to halve the cost and accept a slower answer. effort controls how hard the model thinks: 'low' suits a question asked at the wheel, 'high' suits drafting a rate negotiation.

outlook._comment: Read-only. Lazy connect: Outlook is contacted only when you ask. 'account' is the mailbox to read - Ops@l1truck.com is the operating default for Level 1 Transport. Leave it empty to use whatever Outlook treats as its default store instead. Run JOE_ACCOUNTS.cmd to list the mailboxes in the profile. Calendar is read in DATE order for the range you ask about; mail newest-first; contacts alphabetical by the name shown. This setting reads ONE mailbox. Multi-mailbox support is Email Connection Layer v1, which is approved and not yet built.
outlook._accounts_comment: Approved mailboxes. Read-only - JOE cannot send, delete, move, flag, or modify anything in them. Mail, calendar, and contacts are chosen SEPARATELY because no mailbox is assumed to hold all three: name a connection id in default_mail_source / default_calendar_source / default_contacts_source, or leave one empty to let JOE use the first available mailbox and say which it used. 'account' below is the legacy single-mailbox setting, kept so existing reads keep working.

research._comment: Live web-grounded research through Microsoft 365 Copilot. It reuses the reasoning sign-in - no separate credential. Set provider to 'none' or 'fixture' to fall back; fixture output is always labelled SAMPLE DATA and is never presented as live. PILOT / PREVIEW: the Copilot Chat API is a /beta endpoint.

voice._comment: Speaking and hearing are separate choices. JOE speaks through Windows System.Speech, which does it well. It hears through whichever recognizer is named below. speak_replies=false means JOE never speaks unless you press Speak.
voice._microphone_comment: preferred_microphone names the device JOE records from. With the whisper recognizer this is enforced, not just remembered - JOE binds to that device by name. Leave it empty to follow the Windows default. Windows spells the same headset several ways, so a partial name matches; JOE reports the exact device it settled on.

whisper._comment: Local speech recognition. Nothing is sent anywhere - the model runs on this machine, which is also why it keeps working with no signal. It can be pointed at a named microphone, which Windows System.Speech cannot: on Mike's Bluetooth headset that engine returned no correct words at all, because a headset drops to narrowband when it records. model: tiny, base, small, medium or large-v3 - larger is more accurate and slower, and base is as far as a 2018 laptop CPU should go. compute_type int8 suits a CPU; use float16 on a machine with a GPU. The first run downloads the model and needs a network.

dispatch._comment: No approved Dispatch interface exists on this machine. The port is defined; nothing is connected. Do not point this at Dispatch internals.
